name: Arteriovenous Malformation of the Thoraco-Abdominal-Pelvic Cavity

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Criteria for AVM Diagnosis

criteria.description: Presence of pulsatile mass or bruit in thoraco-abdominal-pelvic region
Demonstration of direct arteriovenous shunting without intervening capillary bed on angiography or MRI
Symptoms related to high-output cardiac failure or localized ischemia in affected regions
Exclusion of other vascular malformations such as hemangiomas or venous malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical signs plus imaging confirmation of arteriovenous shunting
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging modalities; biopsy is generally avoided due to bleeding risk.

searchTerms: vibrating lump in abdomen and pelvis

pathognomonic.notes: Heard on auscultation due to high-flow shunting

searchTerms: symptoms of heart failure with high blood flow
heart failure signs from increased cardiac output
rapid heartbeat and fatigue due to heart strain

common.notes: Due to mass effect or vascular engorgement
Related to ischemia or venous congestion
searchTerms: on and off belly or pelvic pain

occasional.notes: Due to vascular steal or ischemia
Due to nerve compression or ischemia
searchTerms: nerve problems like numbness or tingling

rare.notes: May cause acute abdomen or shock
Leading to localized pain and swelling
searchTerms: thrombosis in veins carrying blood away
infection in abnormal blood vessel area

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in cases with cardiac failure
Normal inflammatory markers unless secondary infection
imaging: Contrast-enhanced MRI showing nidus of tangled vessels with early venous filling
Digital subtraction angiography demonstrating direct arteriovenous shunting
Doppler ultrasound revealing high-velocity turbulent flow
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
Rare association with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) genes
other: Physical examination revealing palpable thrill and bruit
Hemodynamic studies showing increased cardiac output

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of direct arteriovenous shunting on imaging
Slow-flow vascular lesion without arterial involvement

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe abdominal pain indicating hemorrhage
Signs of high-output cardiac failure such as tachycardia and dyspnea
Rapid enlargement of pulsatile mass suggesting rupture or thrombosis
references: Brinjikji W, et al. Arteriovenous malformations of the body: clinical presentation and management. Neurosurg Clin N Am. 2017;28(3):345-356.
